findings: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp: the parallel key pass sets each key's bit with an atomic fetch_or, and any set bit counts as a duplicate, so duplicate keys are always detected and fall back to ScheduleFinalize. That is the same fallback HashJoinRepartitionEvent uses. NULL keys and keys outside the range are skipped, the same as in the serial TemplatedFillSelectionVectorBuild.

GatherTask: each task covers 131072 slots, a multiple of 64 enforced by a static_assert, so no two tasks write the same validity word. FinishBuild allocates each column's validity mask (Initialize/Copy) before the tasks run, so a gathered NULL cannot trigger a lazy, racy mask allocation. Gathering strings and fixed-width values only stores string_t/value into the target slot. Nested payload types are already rejected in CanDoPerfectHashJoin.

Pinning: the build tasks iterate with KEEP_EVERYTHING_PINNED, so the pins move into segment.pinned_handles under its lock. That is the same mechanism the parallel regular HJ finalize uses, so string pointers stay valid. When a task exits early on a duplicate, its pins are dropped, but the regular finalize pins the data again.

physical_hash_join.cpp: the join filters are now created in FinishEvent, once it is known whether the perfect table is used. This still happens before the probe pipeline runs. The empty-HT NO_OUTPUT_POSSIBLE return cannot be skipped because the parallel path needs at least 64k rows.

CanDoPerfectHashJoin: dropping the INNER gate is a general cost heuristic. INNER joins with a range up to 4M now qualify when the keys fill at least half the range, so memory use is comparable to the regular HT. Nothing in the change refers to the workload's queries or data.

FlushFoundMatch (RIGHT join) uses slot_to_row on the parallel path, and slots with a found match always have a key, so every address it writes through is valid. Thread use goes through the normal task scheduler. No settings, tests or timing code are touched.
